summary: A scholar in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and philosophy, Hajime Okayama studied at Kyoto University, the University of Tokyo, Peking University under Xianlin Ji, and CASS. He served at the University of Tokyo (1995–2012) and Chuo Buddhist College (2022).

Hajime Sakurabe specialized in Buddhist studies and Indology, studying at Otani University under Issai Funahashi and Susumu Yamaguchi. He held posts at Nava Nalanda Mahavihara (~1957–1960) and Otani University, where he was professor from 1971 to 1986.

A philosopher who studied at the University of Tokyo, Kyoto University, Berlin, and Freiburg under Kitaro Nishida, Raphael von Koeber, Martin Heidegger, Edmund Husserl, and Heinrich Rickert. He held posts at Tohoku University (1913) and Kyoto University (1919–1945).
A scholar of Buddhist studies who studied under Dōkyō Etan around 1708 and Hakuyūshi around 1710–1711, later teaching Suiō Genro.

A scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy, Hakuju Ui studied at the University of Tokyo under Junjirō Takakusu, and in Tübingen, Cambridge, and Oxford. He held posts at Tohoku, Tokyo, Komazawa (President, 1941), and Nagoya universities.

A scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy, Yasutani studied at Toshima Normal School and trained under teachers including Sogaku Harada (1925–1943) and Bokusan Nishiari. In 1954, he founded Sanbo Zen.
Hakuyu Hadano was a scholar in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He held posts at Tohoku University, attested as assistant professor between 1953 and 1959 and as professor emeritus in 2026.

A specialist in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and history/archaeology, Halle O'Neal completed her PhD at the University of Kansas under Sherry Fowler (attested 2011). She is attested as co-director at the University of Edinburgh in 2026.

A Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Vidyodaya Pirivena, Banaras Hindu University, and the University of Edinburgh. He headed the London Buddhist Vihara (1957–1990) and taught at Banaras Hindu University, SOAS, and the University of Toronto.
Hank Glassman works in the fields of Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies, holding a faculty post at Haverford College (attested in 2009 and 2019).

A scholar in Tibetology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies, Hanna Havnevik held academic posts at the University of Oslo, where she was attested as professor from 2006 to 2008 and as professor emerita in 2026.

A linguist and Indologist, Hanns Oertel completed his doctorate at Yale University under William Dwight Whitney (~1888–1890). He held posts at Yale (1891–1917), the University of Basel, the University of Marburg, and the University of Munich (1925–1935).

An Indologist and Iranian/Central Asian studies scholar, Schmidt earned his PhD at the University of Hamburg under Ludwig Alsdorf. He held posts at Deccan College, Dr. Hari Singh Gour University, Tübingen, and UCLA (1965–2000).
A historian who studied at the University of Bonn (~1869–1873) and served on the faculty at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1883–1921) and Frederick William University Berlin (1885).

Hans Harder is an Indology and religious studies scholar who studied at Hamburg, Heidelberg, and Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg under Rahul Peter Das. He held an assistant post at Halle-Wittenberg (1995–2007) and Heidelberg (2007).

An Indologist who studied at Tübingen, Kirchliche Hochschule Bethel, Munich, and Marburg, earning his PhD under Friedrich Heiler (~1935–1939). His other teachers included Hanns Oertel, Walther Wüst, Ferdinand Sommer, and Kurt Huber.

A scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies and religious studies, Schaeder held professorial posts at the University of Leipzig (~1930–1931), Humboldt University of Berlin (~1931–1946), and the University of Göttingen (~1946–1957).

A linguist and Indologist, Hock studied at Northwestern and Yale under Warren Crawford Cowgill (~1967–1971). He spent his academic career at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign (~1967–2013) as professor of linguistics and Sanskrit.
Hans Krahe was a linguist who held posts at the University of Würzburg (~1936–1946), Heidelberg University (~1946–1949), and the University of Tübingen (~1950–1965).

A scholar of religious studies and philosophy, Küng studied at the Pontifical Gregorian University, Collegium Germanicum et Hungaricum, and the Catholic University of Paris. He held a post at the University of Tübingen from approximately 1960 to 1996.
